screens.name: Fast growers with expanding margins
screens.description: Companies whose sales have grown fast for several quarters running, with the operating margin holding or widening as they grew.
screens.rule: Revenue up more than 20% on the same quarter a year earlier in each of the last four quarters, or up at least 15% in each of the last two with the operating margin at least 2.5 points above a year earlier. A profit after tax in the latest quarter and over the last four. An operating margin of at least 8%, and no more than 1.5 points below a year earlier. At least ₹2 crore traded a day, where the scan has measured it. Banks, lenders and insurers have no operating margin: no margin test is applied to them, so they are listed on the four quarters above 20% alone.
screens.order: In order of two ranks among the companies listed, averaged: revenue growth (the middle figure of the quarters shown) and the change in operating margin on a year earlier (growth alone where there is no margin).

screens.name: Operational turnarounds
screens.description: Back to a profit from a loss a year earlier, on higher sales, with the business itself behind the profit rather than other income or a one-off gain.
screens.rule: A profit after tax in the latest quarter against a loss in the same quarter a year earlier, on higher revenue. EBITDA excluding exceptional items positive and above the same quarter a year earlier. Other income no more than 30% of profit before tax, and exceptional items no more than 25% of it; a loss before tax fails both. Banks, lenders and insurers are not tested on EBITDA or other income: a lender's fees and treasury income are its business.
screens.order: In order of how far the net margin (profit after tax ÷ revenue) moved from a year earlier, so no company is placed first for its size alone.

screens.name: Cash-rich FCF compounders
screens.description: Businesses that have turned their profit into cash year after year, carry little debt and have grown their sales.
screens.rule: Free cash flow positive in each of the last 3 full years, and operating cash flow above profit after tax, itself positive, in the latest. Debt at most 0.3× equity, or more cash and current investments than borrowings. Revenue up at least 8% a year over three years. Return on capital employed at least 15%, where it can be worked out. Banks, lenders and insurers are not listed: their cash flow and debt describe the lending, not the business.
screens.order: In order of free cash flow yield (the latest year's free cash flow ÷ market value) where a price is held; companies without one follow, in order of return on capital employed.
